title: Russia hosts the 16th BRICS summit in Kazan
body:
The 16th BRICS summit was held in Kazan, Russia, from 22 to 24 October 2024, chaired by Russian President Vladimir Putin under the theme "Strengthening Multilateralism for Fair Global Development and Security". Members were Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, together with Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, which had joined at the previous summit. The summit created a new category of partner countries and added 13: Algeria, Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Turkey, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.

Leaders attending in person included Putin, Narendra Modi, Xi Jinping, Cyril Ramaphosa, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Abiy Ahmed, Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammed bin Zayed, while Brazil's Lula took part online. Guests included Mahmoud Abbas, Alexander Lukashenko and Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. UN Secretary-General António Guterres attended and met Putin, which drew criticism from Ukraine's Foreign Ministry and others given the International Criminal Court arrest warrant issued for Putin on 17 March 2023. Zelensky declined to meet Guterres in Kyiv afterwards.

The Kazan Declaration emphasised adherence to the UN Charter and supported diplomatic efforts toward a peaceful resolution of the conflict in Ukraine. Xi and Putin agreed to integrate the Belt and Road Initiative with the Eurasian Economic Union. Modi and Xi held their first formal bilateral meeting in five years and announced a deal to resolve a four-year border standoff through troop disengagement.
